name: Microphone (audio capture)
plain: Asks to turn on the microphone and receive live audio.
meaning: Gives the site live sound from the room: voice, background talk, ambient noise. Used for calls and dictation; also usable for voice biometrics or covert listening if the tab stays open.

access.prompt_ui: Chrome: bubble with Allow while visiting, Allow this time, Don't allow. Firefox: device chooser plus Remember. Safari: Allow or Don't Allow. Tab shows a recording icon (red dot) while active.
access.persistence: Chrome and Edge: persistent per origin until reset; Safari and Firefox: per session unless remembered.
access.revocation: Padlock icon, Site settings, OS microphone privacy settings; track.stop(); tab audio indicator.
steps: MediaStream with an audio track; echoCancellation, noiseSuppression, autoGainControl default on

limits.headline: Can hear and record live audio from your microphone while the tab is open
limits.user_action: You click Unmute, Record, or Join call, then choose Allow in the browser pop up
can: Capture live audio from your microphone
Send that audio to other people on a call or to the site's servers
List your microphones and switch between them once you allow access
cannot: Turn the microphone on the first time without your Allow tap
Keep listening after you close the tab; the tab shows a recording indicator while it runs
Use the microphone if it is blocked in your device settings
Hear other apps or system sound, only what the microphone picks up
limits.differs: Chrome offers Allow this time, Firefox lets you pick a microphone in the pop up, and Safari asks per site.

story.what_it_is: Lets a website listen through your microphone, live.

marketing.name: getUserMedia
marketing.pitch: Developer docs describe how a page asks permission, then streams live microphone audio for calls and dictation.

marketing.name: One-time permissions
marketing.pitch: Chrome describes Allow this time, which gives microphone access for one visit only.

story.for_you: A box asks to use your microphone, and you pick Allow or Block. While it is on, the tab shows a mic icon. The site hears voices and room noise until you close the tab or turn it off.
story.for_makers: The microphone is the heart of web calls, voice chat in games and voice search. A maker can add voice to any web product without an app. It also opens the door to features such as live captions, voice commands and sound checks.

use_cases.example: In a browser or cloud game, you press a button to talk to your squad over voice chat, and the game sends your voice to the team.
You join a Zoom or Google Meet call in a browser tab, allow the mic, and others hear you right away.
A web tuner or music app listens to your guitar or voice and shows if you are in tune or singing the right note.
You hold a mic button in a web chat, speak, and the site sends the voice note.
A language site asks you to say a phrase and scores your pronunciation as you speak.
A person who cannot type well dictates a long email by voice and sees live words appear in the text box.
A phone call center site checks your voice print on a login, using a live clip of your voice as a second factor.

risks: Covert listening from a forgotten tab

technical_bounds: OS and browser show an active indicator
Background tabs on mobile stop capture
Cannot hear system audio (see display-capture systemAudio)

history.change: Tab recording indicator becomes standard in tab strip
